heard: Jean de Valette fired the heads of prisoners from his cannons. In 1565, 40,000 Ottoman soldiers arrived to conquer Malta. Grand Master Valette ordered his men to poison their own wells. When Fort Saint Elmo fell, invaders floated decapitated knights across the bay. Valette retaliated by beheading his prisoners and firing them back. The few survivors held until relief arrived in September. The conflict began when the the massive armada arrived.
